news.headline: Acuff recorded 32 points (11-21 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 7-7 FT), 10 assists, five rebounds and a steal in 39 minutes during Sunday's 114-108 loss to the Heat.
news.story: Acuff continues to impress to begin his rookie campaign, racking up a game-high 32 points. Sunday marked the fourth time Acuff has scored at least 30 points in his first 10 games. The 19-year-old also flashed his playmaking ability, dishing 10 assists to secure his third career double-double. Acuff has scored at least 20 points in each of his last six appearances, averaging 28.8 points, 9.2 assists, 4.5 rebounds and 1.0 steals in 38.2 minutes per contest over that stretch.

news.headline: Acuff finished with 22 points (9-20 FG, 3-9 3Pt, 1-2 FT), three rebounds, eight assists and two steals in 33 minutes during Friday's 124-109 loss to San Antonio.
news.story: Acuff led the Kings in scoring and assists in another encouraging rookie performance. He needed 20 shots to get there, but his ability to create offense has made him one of the bright spots in a rough start for Sacramento. As the Kings lose more games, expect them to keep giving him the ball.

news.headline: Acuff finished Wednesday's 116-103 loss to the Lakers with 22 points (8-24 FG, 3-11 3Pt, 3-4 FT), three rebounds, 12 assists and two steals across 42 minutes.
news.story: Acuff struggled with his efficiency, needing 24 shots to reach 22 points, but he made up for it with a double-double. That extends his streak of games with at least five assists to six. The rookie's heavy usage and team-high 42 minutes make him a fantasy asset even on off shooting nights, though his efficiency could weigh on managers in category leagues.

news.headline: VanVleet finished with 12 points (4-9 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 1-2 FT), a rebound and two assists across 30 minutes in Monday's 110-100 win over the Nuggets.
news.story: VanVleet provided efficient perimeter shooting but struggled to contribute beyond scoring, recording just two assists and no defensive stats. The limited playmaking was disappointing for fantasy managers. VanVleet's three-point production still offers value, but his fantasy reliability depends on generating more assists and steals. Staying under the 20-point threshold with subpar numbers in other categories simply won't cut it in standard leagues.

news.headline: VanVleet tallied 16 points (6-12 FG, 4-9 3Pt), three rebounds, four assists and a block across 31 minutes in Saturday's 102-99 loss to the Suns.
news.story: VanVleet supplied efficient perimeter scoring, recording four three-pointers for the third time in his last five outings while contributing four assists. His established role, both as a playmaker and scorer, and consistent three-point volume continue to provide fantasy utility, particularly in category formats emphasizing assists and perimeter shooting. He's also taken a step forward offensively, as he has overcame a slow start to the campaign to score at least 16 points in four of his last five outings. By all means, the veteran floor general, who missed the entire 2025-26 season while recove

news.headline: VanVleet (knee) isn't listed on the injury report for Monday's game against the Celtics.
news.story: VanVleet took the night off Saturday, which was the second night of a back-to-back set, but will return to action Monday. The veteran has looked solid coming back from an ACL tear, averaging 13.0 points, 6.4 assists, 4.0 rebounds and 1.8 steals in 30.6 minutes per game across his first five appearances.

news.headline: Flagg finished with 43 points (16-25 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 8-8 FT), 11 rebounds, six assists, three steals and one block in 39 minutes during Monday's 125-122 win over Indiana.
news.story: Flagg delivered his best offensive showing of the 2026-27 season so far, beating his previous high of 33 points Oct. 30 against Houston. He also set a season high in rebounds and has now reached double-digit boards three times in 10 matchups. Flagg has now collected four straight double-doubles following Monday's victory.

news.headline: Lendeborg totaled 23 points (8-10 FG, 4-4 3Pt, 3-4 FT), seven rebounds, four assists and one steal over 27 minutes during Monday's 138-87 win over New Orleans.
news.story: Lendeborg was nearly flawless from the field, hitting all four of his three-point attempts. He also filled the box score in just 27 minutes. The rookie continues to look like the Warriors' No. 2 option behind Stephen Curry, and his all-around production should keep him in standard lineups. The lopsided score kept Lendeborg's minutes in check, but he still did plenty even in limited action.

news.headline: Lendeborg notched 23 points (9-15 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 3-4 FT), eight rebounds, three assists and three blocks across 37 minutes in Saturday's 126-119 overtime win over the Magic.
news.story: Lendeborg combined efficient scoring with strong rebounding and rim protection, delivering one of his most complete performances of the season and ending just two boards shy of a double-double. His six turnovers were a drawback, but the 37-minute workload demonstrated Golden State's willingness to rely on him in competitive situations. His versatile statistical profile offers considerable fantasy upside as his role continues to develop, and he remains one of the most productive rookies in this year's class. He's averaging 21.2 points, 7.2 rebounds, 4.0 assists and a combined 1.8 steals-plus-bl

news.headline: Clingan closed with 24 points (9-12 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 5-6 FT), 11 rebounds, one assist, three blocks and one steal over 29 minutes during Wednesday's 132-119 victory over Phoenix.
news.story: The double-double was the second straight for Clingan, while the 24 points were a season high for the third-year center. Clingan also recorded multiple rejections for the fourth time in seven games, and so far in 2026-27, he's averaging 12.0 points, 10.6 boards, 2.4 blocks, 1.6 assists and 1.0 threes while shooting 56.9 percent from the field and a surprising 46.7 percent from long distance.

news.headline: Clingan delivered 17 points (8-16 FG, 1-3 3Pt), 18 rebounds, three assists and four blocks across 32 minutes in Monday's 118-110 win over the Nuggets.
news.story: Clingan delivered an outstanding fantasy performance, grabbing nine offensive rebounds while providing elite rim protection against Denver's frontcourt led by none other than Nikola Jokic. Clingan's combination of rebounding volume and shot-blocking makes him an appealing option at center, and even though he's not likely to hover around the 15-point mark on a regular basis, his floor remains very high due to his two-way contributions.

news.headline: Stirtz ended Saturday's 114-75 victory over the Wizards with 11 points (3-12 FG, 2-8 3Pt, 3-3 FT), five rebounds, two assists and one block over 29 minutes.
news.story: Stirtz saw a career high in playing time in the blowout win, logging 20-plus minutes for the sixth time in Oklahoma City's last seven games. Although the rookie guard struggled with efficiency, he still scored in double figures for a third straight game. Over that span, he's averaged 13.0 points, 2.3 rebounds, 1.7 assists and 1.3 steals across 25.0 minutes per game.

news.headline: Stirtz contributed 16 points (6-9 FG, 4-7 3Pt), one rebound, one assist and two steals in 22 minutes during Wednesday's 124-116 win over the Cavaliers.
news.story: Stirtz provided a significant offensive lift off the bench, establishing a career high in scoring while knocking down four three-pointers. The rookie guard also contributed two steals and avoided committing a turnover. His performance was particularly encouraging with Oklahoma City missing several rotation players, though his long-term fantasy outlook remains tied to the Thunder's backcourt health.

news.headline: Stirtz racked up 11 points (4-8 FG, 3-6 3Pt), one rebound and three assists across 26 minutes during Saturday's 119-98 loss to the Rockets.
news.story: Stirtz gave the shorthanded Thunder a scoring lift off the bench. After a standout preseason, the rookie is finding a steady regular-season role in a depleted backcourt. He isn't doing enough outside of scoring to matter in standard leagues yet, but he's worth watching in deeper formats.

news.headline: Reed will come off the bench Monday against Washington, Eric Vincent of ClutchPoints.com reports.
news.story: Reed averaged 12.1 points, 6.7 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.3 steals in seven straight starts for the Pistons, but the team has elected to make a lineup change Monday. Daniss Jenkins will enter the first unit in Reed's place.

news.headline: Reed produced eight points (4-8 FG, 0-2 FT) and 10 rebounds in 20 minutes during Sunday's 121-116 loss to the Lakers.
news.story: Reed remained in the starting lineup due to Jalen Duren (hamstring) being unavailable, and the former made an impact on the offensive glass, collecting eight of his 10 rebounds on that end. However, Reed's playing time was limited to 20 minutes, and he failed to record a steal or block. The big man offers short-term rebounding upside while Duren is sidelined, but his modest workload limits his fantasy ceiling.

news.headline: Reed racked up 11 points (5-6 FG, 1-2 FT), five rebounds, four assists, two blocks and two steals across 28 minutes during Monday's 124-91 victory over the Hornets.
news.story: Reed turned in another strong two-way performance, filling in for the injured Jalen Duren (hamstring). In four appearances over the past week, he has been a top-30 asset in nine-category leagues, averaging 15.3 points, 5.5 rebounds, 0.8 three-pointers and 3.0 combined steals and blocks. The eventual return of Duren will certainly impact Reed's production. However, given how well the team has functioned with Reed as the starting center, there is a case to be made for him playing over John Collins, alongside Duren.

news.headline: Irving delivered 35 points (11-18 FG, 7-10 3Pt, 6-7 FT) and four assists across 38 minutes in Monday's 125-122 win over the Pacers.
news.story: Irving produced an outstanding offensive performance, connecting on seven three-pointers while shooting efficiently from the field, but his production in other categories was subpar or nonexistent. His four assists show he's now a secondary playmaker behind Cooper Flagg, who notched six assists despite not being the default point guard. Still, Irving's elite shot-making continues to provide substantial fantasy upside, especially when his perimeter shooting reaches this level, but an uptick in assists or more consistent output in other categories would boost his fantasy profile considerably.

news.headline: Irving delivered 21 points (9-15 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 1-1 FT), three rebounds, four assists and one steal across 29 minutes in Sunday's 130-93 win over the Nets.
news.story: Irving produced an efficient scoring performance against his former team, helping Dallas establish a commanding lead before the fourth quarter. His limited workload reflected the lopsided result, not a diminished offensive role. Irving remains a dependable fantasy option even when he's operating as a secondary scorer and playmaker behind star second-year forward Cooper Flagg.

news.headline: Young ended with 20 points (6-17 FG, 3-10 3Pt, 5-9 FT), one rebound, seven assists and two steals across 38 minutes during Monday's 122-111 loss to Detroit.
news.story: Young was inefficient from the field and the free-throw line, but he reached 20 points and led Washington in assists. Playing alongside Anthony Davis and AJ Dybantsa has cut into his scoring opportunities, though Young's role as the primary facilitator keeps his fantasy floor steady.

news.headline: Young finished with four points (1-6 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-3 FT), five rebounds, three assists and one steal in 28 minutes during Saturday's 114-75 loss to the Thunder.
news.story: Young turned in a lackluster all-around performance, delivering his lowest point total in a game since Nov. 4, 2024, when he recorded just two points in 23 minutes. The star floor general also delivered a season low in assists. In four outings so far this month, Young has averaged 15.0 points, 7.0 assists, 3.0 rebounds and 1.3 steals across 33.3 minutes per contest.

news.headline: Young registered 18 points (6-12 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 4-4 FT), two rebounds, six assists, one block and two steals over 34 minutes during Wednesday's 120-105 loss to the Hawks.
news.story: Young delivered a respectable offensive performance against his former team, shooting 50 percent from the field while contributing six assists. However, he committed four turnovers and couldn't prevent Washington from suffering a 15-point defeat. The veteran point guard continues to serve as a primary offensive facilitator for the Wizards, providing a reliable source of points and assists for fantasy managers.

news.headline: Green recorded two points (1-5 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 0-2 FT), six rebounds, 13 assists, two steals and two blocks across 34 minutes in Saturday's 126-119 overtime win over the Magic.
news.story: Green overcame a nearly nonexistent scoring contribution by delivering outstanding playmaking and defensive production. His season-high 13 assists and four combined defensive stats provided substantial category-league value, and it's worth noting he's now dished out double-digit assists in back-to-back games. Green's poor scoring numbers limit his upside, but there's no denying that he's compensating for that with strong numbers in other categories. Over his last five games, Green is averaging 2.6 points, 5.6 rebounds, 8.2 assists, 1.4 steals and 1.2 blocks per contest.

news.headline: Green (elbow) is available for Saturday's game against the Magic.
news.story: Green will power through the elbow issue and make himself available for Saturday's game. The 36-year-old forward is averaging 3.0 points, 5.0 rebounds, 7.0 assists and 1.8 stocks per contest this season.

news.headline: Green (elbow) is listed as questionable ahead of Saturday's game against Orlando.
news.story: Green is coming off an 11-assist performance in Thursday's 120-100 win over the Heat. He's in danger of missing his third contest of the 2026-27 campaign due to elbow inflammation. If Green is downgraded to out, Charles Bassey and Al Horford would likely split time at the five.

news.headline: Nesmith tallied 18 points (5-14 FG, 4-10 3Pt, 4-6 FT), two rebounds, two assists, a steal and a block across 34 minutes in Monday's 125-122 loss to the Mavericks.
news.story: Nesmith connected on four three-pointers while maintaining a substantial workload, but his overall shooting efficiency remained inconsistent. Nesmith remains a useful perimeter scoring option, particularly in deeper category leagues, with his production heavily dependent on three-point volume and defensive contributions. A bit more consistency in the scoring column would go a long way, as he's scored in double digits in six of his last eight games but has surpassed the 15-point threshold only three times in that span.

news.headline: Nesmith registered 16 points (7-16 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 0-1 FT), a rebound, two assists, three steals and a block across 30 minutes in Wednesday's 107-103 win over the Grizzlies.
news.story: Nesmith delivered the decisive three-pointer in the closing seconds, extending Indiana's lead after Memphis pulled within one point. His four combined defensive stats significantly boosted his fantasy production despite modest rebounding and playmaking totals. Nesmith's established playing time and defensive contributions support his value in category formats, although his scoring consistency is dependent on perimeter efficiency. He's trending in the right direction, scoring in double figures in five of his last six appearances.

news.headline: Nesmith (rest) is not listed on the injury report for Wednesday's game in Memphis.
news.story: Nesmith sat out Monday's 108-104 loss to the Hawks for rest purposes, but he'll be back in action Wednesday evening. Nesmith is averaging 12.2 points, 1.8 assists and 1.7 triples per game this season.

news.headline: Zubac posted 16 points (5-7 FG, 6-8 FT) and three rebounds across 28 minutes in Monday's 125-122 loss to the Mavericks.
news.story: Zubac scored efficiently around the basket, converting five of seven field-goal attempts and making six free throws. However, his three rebounds were disappointing for a starting center, and he recorded no defensive stats. Zubac's fantasy value remains closely tied to rebounding and field-goal efficiency, making this a relatively underwhelming performance despite his scoring contribution.

news.headline: Zubac notched 10 points (4-5 FG, 2-2 FT), 12 rebounds and five assists in 19 minutes during Saturday's 114-102 loss to the Nuggets.
news.story: Zubac recorded his second double-double of the season, and his first since returning from an ankle injury that cost him five games. He was dealing with some foul trouble, which may have contributed to him playing just 19 minutes. However, he appears to be trending in the right direction and should approach closer to 30 minutes per game in the not too distant future.

news.headline: Banchero is expected to be sidelined for the next four-to-six weeks due to a right high-ankle sprain, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
news.story: Banchero left during Friday's loss against the Timberwolves due to an ankle injury, and follow-up tests have confirmed a high-ankle sprain for the fifth-year forward. With an extended absence expected, the Magic will have to rely more heavily on Franz Wagner and Desmond Bane offensively, and Tristan da Silva figures to be the top candidate to enter the Magic's starting lineup for as long as Banchero is sidelined.

news.headline: Banchero didn't check back in during the fourth quarter of Friday's 115-93 loss to the Timberwolves after being deemed doubtful to return. He finished with 14 points (5-11 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 2-4 FT), six rebounds, five assists and one steal across 26 minutes.
news.story: Banchero exited to the locker room in the third quarter after tweaking his right ankle. He briefly returned to action in the third but didn't see the floor in the fourth due to ankle soreness. The star forward can be considered questionable for Sunday's game at New York until the Magic offer an update on his status.

news.headline: Banchero is doubtful to return to Friday's game against the Timberwolves due to a sore right ankle, NBA reporter Marc Stein reports.
news.story: The Magic are currently down by 20-plus points with four minutes to go in the fourth quarter, so that may be impacting Orlando's decision to hold Banchero out of the remainder of the game. For now, Banchero should be considered questionable for Sunday's game in New York.

news.headline: Herro (knee) is listed as out for Tuesday's game against New York.
news.story: Herro was listed as questionable ahead of this contest. However, he has been downgraded to out, meaning his next opportunity to suit up will come Wednesday versus the Lakers. With Herro sidelined, Ryan Rollins could enter the starting lineup for the first time since the 136-111 loss to Cleveland on Oct. 31.

news.headline: Herro (knee) is listed as questionable for Tuesday's game against the Knicks.
news.story: Herro exited to the locker room during Sunday's loss to the Celtics after suffering a knee injury, though he later returned to the game. However, he's since been added to the injury report with a right knee contusion. If the veteran guard is ultimately ruled out for the front end of this back-to-back set, Brayden Burries and Ryan Rollins would likely see expanded roles. AJ Green could also see increased playing time if Herro is ruled out.

news.headline: Herro finished with 13 points (5-12 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one rebound and two assists across 27 minutes in Sunday's 117-97 loss to the Celtics.
news.story: Herro had a disappointing offensive outing, connecting on just one of five three-point attempts while contributing little beyond scoring. The veteran guard's scoring and perimeter shooting remain valuable, but his fantasy reliability depends on improved efficiency.

news.headline: Pritchard tallied 12 points (4-10 FG, 4-6 3Pt), six rebounds, five assists and a steal across 23 minutes in Friday's 119-80 win over the Hornets.
news.story: Pritchard made all four of his field goals from beyond the arc to snap an 0-for-12 drought from three in his previous three contests. Inconsistency has been Pritchard's biggest issue so far. He has failed to score more than 12 points in four straight games, but he's also surpassed the 25-point mark twice already. At the end of the day, while his ability to produce across multiple categories remains encouraging, Pritchard's fantasy outlook still depends on his perimeter shooting as his primary source of production.

news.headline: Pritchard (eye) is available for Friday's game against the Hornets, Zack Cox of the Boston Heraldreports.
news.story: Pritchard will shed his questionable tag ahead of this contest after leaving Wednesday's game early. As of Friday afternoon, there's been no mention of restrictions or any limitations health-wise for the veteran point guard.

news.headline: Camara accumulated 18 points (7-12 FG, 4-8 3Pt), six rebounds and one assist in 30 minutes during Friday's 124-118 loss to the Lakers.

When he's making shots from the corner, Portland's starting lineup gets much harder to guard. He's a key piece of the rotation, and nights like this show why he's playing starter minutes.

news.headline: Camara posted 11 points (4-9 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 2-6 FT), four rebounds and two assists across 32 minutes during Wednesday's 132-119 win over the Suns.
news.story: Camara has now scored in double digits in six of his first seven appearances. He'll likely remain a low-end fantasy option, as Camara isn't handling additional usage in Ja Morant's (hamstring) absence.

The star forward also paced the club in rebounds and finished second in assists, dishing out a season-high eight dimes. Siakam has reached the 20-point threshold in three straight games, shooting 57.4 percent from the field over that stretch.

news.headline: Siakam recorded 23 points (10-18 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 1-2 FT), two rebounds and five assists in 32 minutes during Saturday's 114-102 loss to Denver.
news.story: Siakam led all players in scoring with an efficient shooting effort from the field, as he was one of four Pacers who finished with 10 or more points. Siakam has tallied 20-plus points in two consecutive outings, but his lack of defensive stats and a season-low two boards will leave fantasy managers wanting more. However, with Indiana's roster banged up, the 32-year-old should continue to operate as the focal point of the offense.

news.headline: Siakam posted 20 points (8-13 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, two assists, two steals and a block across 30 minutes in Wednesday's 107-103 win over the Grizzlies.
news.story: Siakam delivered an efficient offensive performance while adding three combined defensive stats, helping Indiana snap its five-game losing streak. His 30-minute workload was slightly modest for a primary scoring option, but his balanced contributions supported another productive fantasy outing. Siakam remains a dependable source of points and rebounds, with defensive activity providing additional value.

news.headline: Queta posted 13 points (6-11 FG, 1-2 FT), nine rebounds and four assists across 22 minutes in Sunday's 117-97 win over the Bucks.

news.headline: Karabell's notebook: Harden's declining role, Garland's TOs, a rookie to watch
news.story: It's easy to claim otherwise today, but there was little indication Cleveland Cavaliers PG/SG James Harden would suddenly become a fantasy disappointment this season. news.headline: Brown supplied 30 points (11-19 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 5-7 FT), seven rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block across 37 minutes in Wednesday's 112-106 win over the Pistons.

news.headline: Edgecombe recorded 19 points (8-13 FG, 3-5 3Pt), three rebounds, two assists and four steals over 32 minutes in Friday's 119-95 loss to the Cavs.
news.story: Edgecombe was locked in on both ends of the floor, ripping away a season-high four steals while also scoring with remarkable efficiency. He also finished without committing a single turnover, which was nice to see after he coughed up the rock a season-high three times in his previous outing.

news.headline: McDaniels finished with 16 points (5-9 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 4-4 FT), six rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block across 33 minutes in Sunday's 115-100 win over the Jazz.
news.story: McDaniels delivered an efficient all-around performance, contributing in every major statistical category while maintaining a substantial workload. His two made three-pointers and perfect free-throw shooting strengthened his offensive efficiency, while his defensive contributions provided additional value. McDaniels remains particularly useful in category formats, where his versatility can compensate for inconsistent scoring volume.

news.headline: McDaniels finished with 23 points (8-19 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 5-5 FT), six rebounds, five assists, one steal and two blocks over 40 minutes in Friday's 115-109 win over the Pelicans.
news.story: McDaniels snapped a three-game swat-less streak during Friday's win, and he got some triples to drop after going 0-for-7 from beyond the arc in his previous outing. The 26-year-old vet is off to his best start yet, averaging 17.1 points, 6.2 rebounds, 3.6 assists, 1.4 triples, and 1.7 stocks per contest, which has him flirting with top-50 value on the year.

news.headline: McDaniels finished Wednesday's 117-107 victory over Houston with 14 points (7-14 FG, 0-6 3Pt), eight rebounds, four assists and two steals over 37 minutes.
news.story: McDaniels remains a reliable presence on the wing for Minnesota, having collected at least 13 points and six boards in eight of his first nine appearances. He's averaged 16.4 points, 6.2 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 0.9 steals in 33.2 minutes per game this season.

news.headline: Sengun delivered 20 points (9-17 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 1-3 FT), 11 rebounds, eight assists, a steal and a block across 35 minutes in Monday's 110-100 win over the Nuggets.
news.story: Sengun delivered another outstanding all-around performance, finishing two assists shy of a triple-double while matching Nikola Jokic blow for blow. Sengun's 11 rebounds included five offensive boards, highlighting his impact around the basket, and he fell just one shy of matching his season-high output in that category. Sengun's combination of scoring, rebounding and playmaking continues to provide an excellent fantasy foundation across all formats as one of the best centers in fantasy this season.

news.story: Sengun recorded his first triple-double of the season, albeit in a losing effort. It continues what has been a strong start to the season, as he is currently putting up first-round value in standard leagues. Through seven appearances, he has averaged 22.4 points, 9.1 rebounds, 8.1 assists, 1.0 three-pointers and 2.4 combined steals and blocks.

news.headline: Castle tallied 14 points (5-12 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), seven rebounds, five assists and a block across 24 minutes in Saturday's 125-103 win over the Trail Blazers.
news.story: Castle delivered another well-rounded performance, contributing as a rebounder and facilitator while also posting his fourth consecutive game with 14 or more points. Castle's ability to contribute across several categories supports a strong fantasy floor in most formats. He's averaging 16.5 points, 6.3 rebounds and 4.8 assists per game since going scoreless in a win over the Timberwolves on Oct. 31.

news.headline: Castle had 19 points (7-13 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 4-5 FT), three rebounds and seven assists over 28 minutes during Friday's 124-109 win over Sacramento.
news.story: Castle was San Antonio's most active playmaker, finishing with a team-high seven assists alongside his 19 points. The former Rookie of the Year keeps growing as a lead guard, and his pairing with Dylan Harper in the backcourt gives the Spurs two young ball-handlers who can attack the basket.

news.headline: Williams will start Monday's game against the Hawks.
news.story: With Austin Reaves (illness) and Quentin Grimes (finger) sidelined, Williams will join the first unit for the first time since Oct. 27. In four starts this season, he's averaged 11.3 points, 3.0 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.5 steals across 28.5 minutes per tilt.

news.headline: Williams accumulated eight points (3-5 FG, 2-4 3Pt), three rebounds, one assist and two steals over 20 minutes during Friday's 124-118 win over the Trail Blazers.
news.story: Williams gave the Lakers useful minutes off the bench, knocking down a pair of three-pointers and picking up two steals in his 20 minutes. The forward missed three straight games with soreness in his left foot, an issue going back to the preseason, before being cleared to return earlier in the week. The Lakers begin a back-to-back Sunday, so he could be held out for one of those games.

news.headline: Williams contributed 10 points (3-7 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT), four rebounds, one assist and two steals in 23 minutes during Wednesday's 116-103 victory over the Kings.
news.story: After beginning the year as a starter, Williams seems to be getting eased back into action following a recent absence. He'll continue competing with Jake LaRavia for the Lakers' fifth starting lineup position.

news.headline: Watson provided 12 points (5-11 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), six rebounds, three assists, two blocks and one steal over 29 minutes during Saturday's 109-97 loss to the Knicks.
news.story: Watson racked up three stocks after failing to record any defensive statistics his last time out, and this was his second straight game without committing a single turnover. He's been a steady late-round producer on the season with averages of 11.3 points, 4.9 rebounds, 2.8 assists, 1.0 steals and 1.6 blocks per game.

news.headline: Watson (hamstring) is available for Friday's meeting with the 76ers.
news.story: Watson is back after a two-game absence, and his return will likely shift Tyrese Proctor back to the second unit. Watson is averaging 10.8 points, 4.0 rebounds, 3.0 assists, 1.2 steals and 1.8 blocks per game this season.

news.headline: Watson (hamstring) is questionable for Friday's game against the 76ers.
news.story: Watson has missed his team's last two matchups due to a hamstring issue, and he's in danger of missing a third Friday. More information on his availability should come to light as tipoff nears.

news.headline: Clayton produced six points (2-6 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 1-2 FT), six rebounds, four assists, one block and one steal across 25 minutes during Monday's 125-122 win over Indiana.
news.story: After being cut loose by Memphis during the preseason, Clayton is carving out a solid role for himself in the Dallas backcourt. Over his past five appearances, the 2025 first-rounder is averaging 10.2 points, 4.2 rebounds, 3.8 assists and 1.2 steals in 21.6 minutes per game.

news.headline: Clayton finished Monday's 115-100 loss to the Kings with 20 points (6-9 FG, 4-5 3Pt, 4-4 FT), one rebound, two assists and one steal across 24 minutes.
news.story: Clayton tied Daniel Gafford for the team lead in scoring, providing an efficient offensive spark while Dallas struggled from beyond the arc. With Kyrie Irving (knee) sidelined and Max Christie exiting with a hip injury, Clayton benefited from additional backcourt opportunities. He could have short-term streaming appeal if either guard misses more time, though his role will be less secure once Dallas gets healthier.

news.headline: Clayton registered 15 points (6-7 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 1-1 FT), four rebounds, four assists and a block across 17 minutes in Monday's 113-109 win over the Heat.
news.story: Clayton made the most of his limited opportunities, missing just one of his seven field-goal attempts while adding decent contributions in other categories during a 17-minute cameo. Clayton will likely need more consistent playing time to become a reliable option, but this outing was undoubtedly a step in the right direction.

news.headline: Toppin supplied 11 points (3-6 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 4-4 FT), five rebounds and one assist across 19 minutes during Wednesday's 107-103 victory over the Grizzlies.
news.story: In his return from a three-game absence, Toppin delivered efficient scoring in a reserve role, making half his field-goal attempts and converting all four free throws. However, he committed three turnovers and didn't register a defensive statistic, limiting his overall fantasy contribution. With Pascal Siakam entrenched in the starting lineup and Indiana utilizing several frontcourt options, Toppin remains a situational option in deeper leagues.

news.headline: Toppin (back) is available for Wednesday's game against the Grizzlies.
news.story: Toppin has missed the last three games due to a back injury, though he will return Wednesday against Memphis. As a result, Larry Nance will presumably see fewer minutes. Toppin is having a quality 2026-27 campaign, averaging a career-best 15.2 points and 5.2 rebounds along with 1.2 steals over 22.8 minutes per contest.

news.headline: Toppin (back) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Grizzlies.
news.story: Toppin was available for emergency purposes Monday against the Hawks, so he figures to have a good chance of playing Wednesday. The Pacers should update his status closer to tipoff.

news.headline: George (ankle) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Heat.
news.story: George sustained a right ankle sprain in Sunday's loss to Minnesota and will be sidelined for the front end of this back-to-back set. His next opportunity to play will come Wednesday against Orlando, and the 23-year-old's absence should open up additional minutes for guys like Isaiah Collier and Svi Mykhailiuk. Moreover, Darryn Peterson figures to take on additional on-ball duties.

news.headline: George will not return to Sunday's game against the Timberwolves due to a right ankle injury.
news.story: George suffered a right ankle injury during the fourth quarter of Sunday's game and will not return. He concluded the contest with 19 points (5-13 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 9-10 FT), eight assists, five rebounds and two steals in 29 minutes. George should be considered doubtful for Tuesday's game against the Heat, given the amount of pain he was in after sustaining the injury.

news.headline: George (illness) is available for Sunday's game against the Timberwolves, Shreyas Laddha of The Salt Lake Tribune reports.
news.story: George was listed as questionable ahead of Sunday's contest due to an illness, but he will officially be able to suit up. Over his last five appearances, he holds averages of 20.2 points, 5.0 assists, 4.4 rebounds and 1.0 steals in 32.8 minutes per game.

news.headline: Doncic contributed 32 points (11-22 FG, 3-11 3Pt, 7-7 FT), 10 assists, eight rebounds, five steals and two blocks across 39 minutes in Monday's 124-114 win over Atlanta.
news.story: Doncic returned from a one-game absence due to lower-back tightness and poured in 32 points on 22 shots in the absence of Austin Reaves (illness). Doncic led all players in points, assists and steals while tying the game high in blocks, and the superstar nearly recorded his first triple-double of the campaign. He's reached the 30-point mark in each of his last eight appearances and has posted at least five rebounds and five assists in all 10 of his regular-season games this season.

news.headline: Doncic (back) is off the injury report for Monday's game against Atlanta, per Dave McMenamin of ESPN.com.
news.story: After sitting out Sunday's matchup in Detroit, Doncic is good to go for the second half of this back-to-back set. The MVP candidate is on an absolute tear, having dropped at least 40 points in six of his last seven appearances.

Larsson's combination of three-point shooting and defensive contributions offers some fantasy appeal in deeper formats, particularly if he continues receiving minutes in the upper 20s.

news.story: The veteran wing is re-discovering the long-range shooting form that previously seemed to be left behind in Golden State. He pieced together an incredibly efficient 40-plus point performance, needing only 21 attempts from the field to set his best scoring mark of the young season. Davis also crashed the boards to secure a double-double for the third time in his last four appearances.

news.headline: Davis (ankle) will play Monday against the Pistons.
news.story: The Wizards considered Davis a true game-time decision after missing two straight games with an ankle injury, but he's managed to prove his health prior to tipoff. He's looked sharp in his last five matchups, averaging 25.0 points, 9.4 rebounds, 1.6 assists, 1.4 steals and 1.2 blocks in 33.6 minutes per contest.

news.story: Podziemski delivered efficient perimeter shooting and valuable defensive production while playing a season-high 39 minutes, but with his workload sitting firmly at around 33 minutes per game, his role on offense is pretty much set in stone as a multi-category contributor who can hit threes. His scoring ceiling still depends on shot volume in Golden State's offense, but his contributions in other categories are a nice boost, even if they are inconsistent at times.

news.headline: Podziemski provided nine points (3-8 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 1-2 FT), six rebounds, three assists, one block and one steal across 32 minutes during Thursday's 120-100 win over the Heat.
news.story: Podziemski struggled to find his shooting touch but contributed in several other categories while logging the most minutes of any Golden State player. The fourth-year guard added two triples and a pair of defensive stats, helping compensate for his single-digit scoring output. His substantial workload and versatility provide a useful fantasy floor, though his offensive production remains inconsistent.

news.story: Spencer made his presence felt as a facilitator, leading both teams with nine assists while adding six rebounds in an efficient performance off the bench. He committed just two turnovers and continues to provide Memphis with a reliable secondary playmaking option. Although his scoring output remains modest, Spencer's passing production gives him some appeal in deeper fantasy formats.

news.headline: Coward tallied 23 points (8-19 FG, 4-12 3Pt, 3-4 FT), nine rebounds, four assists and four steals over 33 minutes in Wednesday's 107-103 loss to the Pacers.
news.story: Coward was coming off back-to-back 10-point performances, but he was much more aggressive seeking out his own shot Wednesday and cracked the 20-point plateau for the first time this season. He'll look to keep his momentum going into Friday's meeting with the Thunder.

news.headline: Coward logged 10 points (3-6 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-4 FT), nine rebounds and three assists over 31 minutes during Monday's 135-134 overtime loss to the Pelicans.
news.story: Coward fell just one rebound short of what would have been his third double-double of the season, although as a whole, this was a somewhat underwhelming performance. Despite some inconsistencies, Coward has cobbled together a strong start to the season, averaging 12.8 points, 8.7 rebounds, 2.5 assists, 1.2 steals and 2.5 three-pointers, good enough for borderline top-50 value.

news.headline: Peterson delivered 26 points (11-21 FG, 4-8 3Pt), six rebounds, four assists and a steal across 35 minutes in Sunday's 115-100 loss to the Timberwolves.
news.story: Peterson carried a substantial offensive workload, attempting a team-high 21 shots, and he seems to be finding his footing offensively while scoring at least 20 points in back-to-back games for the first time in his career. The rookie's current playing time and newfound prominent scoring role remain encouraging indicators for his fantasy outlook. He's also surpassed the 15-point mark in four of his last six outings, averaging 17.0 points per game in that stretch.

news.headline: Peterson delivered 21 points (6-12 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 6-6 FT), two rebounds, five assists, two steals and three blocks across 30 minutes in Friday's 112-100 loss to the Mavericks.
news.story: Peterson produced an impressive two-way performance, supplementing efficient scoring with five combined defensive stats. His five assists also highlighted his growing contributions as a playmaker. The rookie's ability to contribute in several categories gives him intriguing fantasy upside, particularly if he maintains a consistent workload near 30 minutes. He's scored at least 14 points in four of his last six games, averaging 15.0 points, 4.0 rebounds, 4.8 assists, 1.3 steals and 1.2 blocks per contest.

news.story: The veteran wing is re-discovering the long-range shooting form that previously seemed to be left behind in Golden State. Thompson's drained multiple three-points in five straight games and poured in at least seven in three of those contests, averaging 21.6 points, 5.6 treys, 2.8 assists, 1.6 boards and 1.0 blocks over that span while shooting a blistering 50.0 percent from beyond the arc, and 52.8 percent from the floor.

news.headline: Thompson closed with 11 points (3-10 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 3-3 FT), three assists and two blocks over 23 minutes during Thursday's 120-100 loss to the Warriors.
news.story: Thompson received a warm reception in his return to Golden State but struggled to find his shooting rhythm, connecting on just two of seven attempts from beyond the arc. The veteran guard was coming off a game-winning three-pointer against the Clippers on Wednesday but couldn't sustain that momentum. His two blocks provided an unexpected fantasy boost, though his value remains heavily dependent on perimeter shooting.

news.headline: Doncic contributed 32 points (11-22 FG, 3-11 3Pt, 7-7 FT), 10 assists, eight rebounds, five steals and two blocks across 39 minutes in Monday's 124-114 win over Atlanta.
news.story: Doncic returned from a one-game absence due to lower-back tightness and poured in 32 points on 22 shots in the absence of Austin Reaves (illness). Doncic led all players in points, assists and steals while tying the game high in blocks, and the superstar nearly recorded his first triple-double of the campaign. He's reached the 30-point mark in each of his last eight appearances and has posted at least five rebounds and five assists in all 10 of his regular-season games this season.

news.headline: Doncic (back) is off the injury report for Monday's game against Atlanta, per Dave McMenamin of ESPN.com.
news.story: After sitting out Sunday's matchup in Detroit, Doncic is good to go for the second half of this back-to-back set. The MVP candidate is on an absolute tear, having dropped at least 40 points in six of his last seven appearances.

news.story: George bounced back emphatically from Friday's eight-point performance, shooting 61.1 percent from the field while matching his season high with five made three-pointers. The veteran forward has now scored at least 25 points in two of his last three appearances, connecting on 12 triples during that stretch. Although his peripheral production was limited Sunday, George's scoring efficiency and three-point volume continue to bolster his fantasy value.

news.headline: George registered eight points (3-11 FG, 2-5 3Pt), five rebounds, an assist, a steal and two blocks across 22 minutes in Friday's 119-80 win over the Hornets.
news.story: George struggled offensively, scoring a season-low eight points on 11 shots, but his defensive contributions helped salvage some fantasy value. George's ability to contribute defensive stats remains valuable, but his fantasy ceiling depends on improved shooting efficiency and consistent offensive involvement. news.story: The 14 boards led all players on the night, but the Kings didn't give enough offensive support to rookie Darius Acuff and his game-high 32 points to actually secure a win. news.headline: Achiuwa (ankle) is available for Wednesday's game against the Lakers.
news.story: Achiuwa was previously listed as probable for the Kings, but he will push through his ankle soreness Wednesday. He's off to a great start this season with averages of 11.6 points, 6.6 rebounds, 1.3 assists, 1.9 steals and 1.0 blocks over 28.6 minutes per contest.

news.headline: Kessler recorded 21 points (8-12 FG, 5-6 FT), 10 rebounds, four assists, one block and one steal in 30 minutes during Monday's 124-114 victory over the Hawks.
news.story: Kessler was efficient around the rim and posted his sixth double-double over the past seven games. He scored at least 20 points for the third time this year and the first time since back-to-back such performances to begin the campaign. His rebounding and efficiency have made him one of the more pleasant surprises in fantasy so far, even on a night when his shot-blocking was quieter than usual.

news.headline: Kessler supplied 12 points (5-10 FG, 2-3 FT), 16 rebounds, four assists, three blocks and one steal over 29 minutes during Sunday's 121-116 win over the Pistons.
news.story: Kessler delivered an excellent all-around performance, grabbing seven offensive rebounds while leading both teams with 16 boards. The center also anchored the Lakers' interior defense with three blocks and contributed four assists, showcasing his versatility beyond the traditional big-man categories. Kessler's combination of rebounding, efficient scoring and rim protection makes him a strong fantasy option, particularly in category leagues.
